column1: Climbing Stairs — n stairs; you can climb 1 or 2 at a time; return number of distinct ways to reach the top. Example: n=2 → 2 (1+1, 2); n=3 → 3 (1+1+1, 1+2, 2+1).
column2: PATTERN: Fibonacci DP. | INSIGHT: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). | STEPS: 1) a=1, b=1. 2) For _ in range(n): a,b = b, a+b. 3) Return a. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Use rolling variables, not an array — this is a textbook Fibonacci.

column1: House Robber — given int array `nums` (each is money in a house), return max amount you can rob with the constraint that no two adjacent houses can be robbed. Example: [1,2,3,1] → 4; [2,7,9,3,1] → 12.
column2: PATTERN: 1D DP with two rolling states. | INSIGHT: At each i, choose: rob (skip prev: prev2 + nums[i]) or skip (prev1). | STEPS: 1) prev2=0, prev1=0. 2) For x in nums: cur=max(prev1, prev2+x); prev2=prev1; prev1=cur. 3) Return prev1. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Two rolling vars suffice — no need for a full DP array.

column1: Word Break — given string s and dict `wordDict`; return True if s can be segmented into a sequence of one or more dictionary words. Example: s='leetcode', wordDict=['leet','code'] → True; s='applepenapple', wordDict=['apple','pen'] → True; s='catsandog', wordDict=['cats','dog','sand','and','cat'] → False.
column2: PATTERN: 1D DP over prefixes. | INSIGHT: dp[i]=True if s[:i] can be segmented. dp[i] = OR over j<i of (dp[j] AND s[j:i] in dict). | STEPS: 1) words=set(wordDict); dp=[False]*(n+1); dp[0]=True. 2) For i in 1..n: for j in 0..i-1: if dp[j] and s[j:i] in words: dp[i]=True; break. 3) Return dp[n]. | TIME/SPACE: O(n²·L) / O(n). | PITFALL: Optimization: limit the j scan to i-max_word_length.

column1: Coin Change — given coin denominations and `amount`, return the min number of coins to make amount, or -1 if impossible. Example: coins=[1,2,5], amount=11 → 3 (5+5+1); coins=[2], amount=3 → -1.
column2: PATTERN: Unbounded knapsack DP (bottom-up). | INSIGHT: dp[a] = min coins for amount a; dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a-c] for c in coins if c<=a). | STEPS: 1) dp=[inf]*(amount+1); dp[0]=0. 2) For a in 1..amount: for c in coins: if c<=a: dp[a]=min(dp[a], dp[a-c]+1). 3) Return -1 if dp[amount]==inf else dp[amount]. | TIME/SPACE: O(amount·#coins) / O(amount). | PITFALL: Greedy fails for arbitrary denominations; must DP. dp[0]=0 is the base.

column1: Longest Increasing Subsequence — given int array, return the length of the longest STRICTLY increasing subsequence. Example: [10,9,2,5,3,7,101,18] → 4 ([2,3,7,101]); [0,1,0,3,2,3] → 4.
column2: PATTERN: O(n²) DP or O(n log n) patience-sort with binary search. | INSIGHT (O(n log n)): Maintain `tails`: tails[i] = smallest possible tail of any increasing subseq of length i+1. For each x, replace via bisect_left (or append). | STEPS: 1) tails=[]. 2) For x in nums: i=bisect_left(tails, x); if i==len(tails): tails.append(x); else tails[i]=x. 3) Return len(tails). | TIME/SPACE: O(n log n) / O(n). | PITFALL: tails is NOT a valid LIS itself — only its LENGTH is the answer. For strictly-increasing use bisect_left; for non-strict use bisect_right.
